transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
- Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Giles Snyder.
The balance of power in the nation's capital
has shifted dramatically following a sweeping series
of democratic victories in the midterm elections.
Democrats have taken control of Congress,
setting up a potentially contentious final two years
of President Trump's term.
NPR's Winster Johnston is in the studio
with a closer look at some of the key Senate races.
- Well, Giles, one of the night's biggest upsets
came in Texas, where Democrat James Tallarico
defeated Republican Ken Paxton.
- We just proved that all the money in the world
is no match for the people of Texas.
(crowd cheering)
- Well, Tallarico is the first Democrat elected
to the U.S. Senate from Texas since 1988.
Turning to Michigan Senate race,
Democrats have won there.
Abdul El-Sayed defeated Republican Mike Rogers.
El-Sayed ran on a progressive platform
promising to put working families
and their economic struggles at the center of his agenda.
- Shouldn't be this hard to buy a second bag of groceries
or fill your tank.
Shouldn't be this hard to afford a home.
It shouldn't be this hard to see a doctor
in the richest, most powerful country in the world.
It shouldn't be this hard to pay your taxes
and know that that money's gonna be spent
on you and your kids instead of dropping bombs
on somebody else and their kids.
(crowd cheering)
- Democrats have also flipped Republican-held Senate seats
in Kansas, Iowa, Ohio, North Carolina, and South Carolina,
and we're still waiting for the results to come in
from the Mississippi and Alaska Senate races.
Now, the outcome of this election
now leaves President Trump facing a Democratic Congress
with potential consequences for his legislative agenda.
And really, the big question now
is whether the president and congressional Democrats
can find common ground or spend the next two years at odds.
- As far as the House of Representatives,
Democrats flipped more than 20 seats to win control
of the House and full control of Congress.
NPR's Barbara Spunt reports that Democrats rode the blue wave
and now bring in an air of divided government.
- Democrats sought to capitalize
on voters' economic frustration this cycle,
pointing to high prices for gas and consumer goods.
Their victory aligns with historic trends
that the party out of power
gained seats in midterm elections.
For months, talk of a blue wave
appeared to grow bigger and bigger,
prompting President Trump to campaign on the ground
in states he previously won handily.
Come January, Democrats will control subpoena power
and will likely conduct investigations
into the Trump administration.
Several Democrats have suggested it may not be
in their best interest to pursue impeachment
against the president for a third time,
but they may well begin impeachment proceedings
into Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
Barbara Spunt, NPR News, Washington.
- And from Washington, this is NPR News.
Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms made history in Georgia
as the first black woman elected governor
in the state and the country.
She defeated GOP candidate for governor,
Rick Jackson, late Tuesday night.
Here are my events from member station WABE and Atlanta reports.
- Democratic governor-elect Bottoms secured
nearly 55% of the vote over Jackson,
a healthcare entrepreneur.
Bottoms also broke the Republican
24-year stronghold on the seat.
Here she is at her election night
watch party in downtown Atlanta.
- Georgia, we sent a message loud and clear
(crowd cheering)
that we want a leader who will put Georgia first
and who will stand up to all the chaos
coming out of Washington, D.C.
- She served one term as Atlanta's 60th mayor,
then served as a senior advisor
in the Biden administration before her run for governor.
The governor-elect will replace Republican Brian Kemp
who served two terms officially taking the seat in January.
For NPR News, I'm Dora my events in Atlanta.
- In addition to Keisha Lance Bottoms in Georgia
and Abdul Al Sayed in Michigan,
Democrats scored other first voters in New Mexico.
We elected Deb Holland to the governor's office,
making her the first Native American woman
to lead a state, David Crowley,
said to become Wisconsin's first black governor.
Voters headed to the polls Tuesday,
largely gloomy over the economy,
but U.S. employers ramped up their job postings in September.
The Labor Department said Tuesday that U.S. job openings
jumped to seven and a half million
from a revised 7.1 million in August.
This is NPR News.

Democrat Abdul El-Sayed defeats Republican Mike Rogers in Michigan Senate race on progressive platform
Democrats flip Republican-held Senate seats in Kansas, Iowa, Ohio, North Carolina, and South Carolina; Mississippi and Alaska pending
Democrats flip more than 20 House seats, gaining control of the House and full control of Congress
Democrats gain subpoena power, may investigate Trump administration; possible impeachment proceedings against Pete Hegseth
Keisha Lance Bottoms wins Georgia governor's race, becoming first Black woman elected governor in the state
Deb Haaland elected New Mexico governor, becoming first Native American woman to lead a state
